summary: Marcel Mauss worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Bordeaux, EPHE, Leiden, Utrecht, and Oxford under Durkheim, Meillet, Lévi, and Foucher. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901, 1914–1940) and Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at EPHE (1938–1963) and served as chief editor of Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
Marco Walther is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He studied at Nagoya University under Yasuhisa Matsumura and at the University of Würzburg under Huinan Yang. His posts include Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and was a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, completing his dissertation under doctoral supervisor Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at the University of Sheffield and held an academic post there from approximately 1984 to 2011.

Margaret Dornish works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead studied at Barnard and Columbia University under Franz Boas. Her career included posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), Fordham University (1968–1970), and the University of Rhode Island (1970).

Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union. She held posts at Harvard (1978–1996) and served as dean at the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and conducted postdoctoral studies under Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya studied at St. Petersburg University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology, she was a researcher and manuscript curator at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from 1956 to 2021.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She was appointed Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Krzysztof Byrski is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Warsaw from 1955 to 1960. He served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw (~1990–1993) and held a post at Civitas University.

Marian Ury specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at the University of California, Davis (1969–1995).

Marianne Pieper studied at the Hamburger Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Politik and completed her habilitation at Magdeburg. She held posts at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and was a professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg (1996–2015).

Marianne Winder worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, University of Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. She held posts at Nottingham, the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies, and the Wellcome Institute.
Marie G. Wanek studied in the fields of Indology and philosophy at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.
